Failed backup of the transaction log for SQL Server database 'EMIS_EIE_SouthTees_Upgrade' from 'STAS822\STAS820\MSSQLSERVER'.
Apr 29, 2026, 1:53:47 PM
Error code
RBK20200004
What happened?
The transaction log chain is broken for database STAS822\EMIS_EIE_SouthTees_Upgrade.
Possible cause
The last transaction log backup, '<unnamed log backup>', was performed outside of a Rubrik CDM instance (Last log backup user: 'XSTEES\SASymphony').
Possible solution
Check with the SQL Server administrator to confirm whether any log backup operations are performed outside of a Rubrik CDM instance. If so, start a new log chain by taking an On-demand snapshot for this database.
In SQL Server, each log backup captures only the transactions that have occurred since the immediately preceding log backup. If two systems (e.g., SQL Agent and a third-party backup system like Rubrik) are both taking log backups it fragments the log chain, making data recovery extremely difficult and unreliable.

description:
Can we please have a full audit on access to the below patient between the below dates:
D1215682
01/06/2022 - 04/06/2026

Hi team, 

Following recent guidance from NHSE, EEMAC is a new NHS England model of care allowing Emergency Medicine teams to manage selected patients beyond the traditional 4 hour standard within an ambulatory setting, while remaining under Emergency Medicine clinical responsibility.

National guidance is explicit that EEMAC is not an admission and remains part of the ED pathway, but that the 4 hour Emergency Care Standard (ECS) clock should stop at the point of transfer into EEMAC, while overall time under Emergency Medicine oversight must still be tracked to ensure patients do not remain in EEMAC in excess of 8 hours. For now the attendance type will remain the same, but in the future it is likely that EEMAC will be type 5 activity recording.

https://www.england.nhs.uk/long-read/extended-emergency-medicine-ambulatory-care-eemac-operating-principles/

At present we have no current workflow in Symphony that supports EEMAC reporting

We have two options proposed which will support the Trust in capturing this data and a third option that we are hoping you could provide knowledge and insight on. 

Option 1 – is it possible within the existing SJUH/LGI department builds within symphony, to create an EEMAC care group, which would stop the 4hr ECS clock, i.e. if the patient was moved at 2hrs, the patient would show as being seen, treated and discharged within 4hrs, and therefore not a breach, but the overall time in dept. clock would continue to count so that we can ensure the patient doesn’t spend longer than 12hrs on EEMAC.

Option 2 – build a new department for EEMAC, for LGI and SJUH, with type 5 activity reporting and ECDS reporting

Option 3 – Optum / EMIS guidance - Have you created EEMAC requirements for any other sites following this guidance. If so, how was this achieved it? Are you able to share what has worked well in other Trusts?

Functional Requirement 

• Ability to record transfer from ED to EEMAC as a discrete, time stamped event.
• Automatic stop of the 4 hour ECS clock at the point of EEMAC transfer.
• Continued tracking of total Emergency Medicine time, including:
o Time in ED
o Time in EEMAC
• Automated alerts/escalation when:
o Time in EEMAC approaches 8 hours
• Maintenance of continuous ECDS data capture, including:
o Tests, investigations, procedures
o Diagnoses and outcomes
• Recording of EEMAC location / care area for reporting and audit.
Data & Reporting Requirements
• Differentiation between:
o Standard ED attendances
o ED ? EEMAC pathway patients
• Ability to report:
o Volume of EEMAC activity
o Time spent in EEMAC
o Outcomes (discharge, admission, transfer back to ED)
• Alignment with ECDS, without breaking current SUS submissions.

Any guidance on workstreams undertaken by other Trusts would be incredibly useful.

It may be beneficial to set up a meeting to discuss this in further detail. 

Many thanks 

Megan Gregory
